system.summary: Index numbers select the number alphabet for the run that follows (62: table 1, a-i = 37..29, k-z = 14..28; 13: table 2, a-i = 38..46, n 61, o 60, r 57, s 56, u 54), with three-digit code numbers for names; the same family as targets/zobel1629, a different key.
system.sibling_key: targets/zobel1629 (Johan Zobel, Paris 1629): same index-switching family, different numbers. Not used to read these letters.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = letter values in the decoder's tables (24 in table 1, 14 in table 2), not signs seen. nomenclator.entries 0 is a placeholder: no code is solved. unread_groups = distinct code numbers in the two transcriptions (9 Vienna, 7 Glückstadt; 165 not counted). homophones: none in key v1; a second value for o (28) is suspected in the Glückstadt letter, not applied. A later key state (v2, key_history/) reads 64, 12, 10 as index numbers from a gloss and adds a third table; not used.

solution.what: Catalogue 2543 (sweep of 11 Nov 2026): unit 260651 images 37-38 viewed at full size; number cipher inside German clear text; no decipherment on or beside the leaves.

While transcribing the Vienna letter (b106), runs after 62 gave 'einige reale dienste' with a rule alphabet (a-i 37 down to 29, k-z 14 up to 28); runs after 13 gave 'sache', 'Fridericus' with a second table (a-i 38 up). Key found before the freeze (declared). Transcription frozen 04:11:09 UTC, md5 953fd409.
Vienna decoded once: 33 units, 17 S, 15 E (13 codes, 2 declared), 1 N: strict 17/33 = 51.52%; letter words only 17/20 = 85.00%. Below 65%: read in part.
Vienna: 5,000 shuffled keys, German 4-gram: 0 reach the true score (true -2.4750; best -3.4441 at seed 20261112; -3.4529 at seed 7, added 13 Nov). Short text.

b110: unit 260651 images 20-110 screened for more Pentz-family cipher: none fresh; a code 165 on image 38 left, line 1, missed by the frozen transcription: with it counted, 17/34 = 50.00%. Key v2 made from a gloss on Günther's letter (image 48); not applied here.

b157: Pentz's Glückstadt relations (unit 274999) image 2, a whole page of figures 14-37 with codes; key v1 table 1 applied unchanged (reader not blind: had tried it on line 1 before the freeze; frozen 13:30:55 UTC, md5 1e70795f). Decoded once: 68 units, 25 S, 31 E, 12 N: strict 25/68 = 36.76%. German: Hamburg, admiral, Norway, provisions, constables, fortress.
Glückstadt: 5,000 shuffled keys, German 4-gram (Simplicissimus): 0 reach the true score at both seeds (true -5.4767; best -6.7301 seed 20261112, -6.5759 seed 7).

Fridericia II p. 17 n. 1 cites Pentz and Hagen to Christian IV of 26 and 30 March 1636 (Bremen Nr. 29, 30 a) and paraphrases the talks: risk on content, no decipherment. Bricka and Fridericia II and IV searched: no print of either letter. Ny kgl. Saml. Fol. 616c not checked.

Folder rebuild (b190): both decodes reproduced byte for byte from the frozen files; every figure reproduced by scripts/build.py; the filed shuffle lines reproduced; the b157 'code units 11' corrected to 10 codes plus one fragment.

outcome.method_basis: The key was found from the ciphertext of the Vienna letter itself (rule alphabets fitted to word runs while transcribing, before the freeze), with no decipherment on or beside it; the clear German around the runs is context. The Glückstadt letter was then decoded with table 1 of that key unchanged. Neither text reaches the contributor's own 65% line.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.txt (scripts/build.py), per document, never pooled: Vienna 17/33 = 51.52% (first pass, of record; 17/34 = 50.00% with the missed code 165); Glückstadt 25/68 = 36.76% (first pass, of record; 23/68 = 33.82% with doubtful figures as holes). fraction_read is the Vienna figure, the catalogued document.

texts.label: Christian Pentz to Christian IV, Vienna, 26 Mar / 5 Apr 1636
texts.summary: Pentz, sent to the Emperor in early 1636 to offer Christian IV's mediation and press Duke Frederik's claim to Bremen, writes in cipher that he has not yet touched on the [168] matter, that real services will be hard to obtain, and that he wishes 'Fridericus' were with the King again; the cipher words sit in clear German that is transcribed only around them.

reading_review.by: Claude (Anthropic), for Malcolm McBratney: a model reading, not a person, and not independent (sessions of the same project). The reviewer's own record should replace it.
reading_review.note: The cipher words fit their clear clauses (einige reale dienste swer zu erhalten sein; Fridericus wider bei euer Mt. were); thirteen codes unread; the clear text is only partly transcribed.

texts.note: read_share is the strict first-pass share: 17 of 33 units (51.52%); 17/34 with the missed code 165.

texts.label: Christian Pentz (Glückstadt) to Christian IV, c.1629-30, image 2 recto
texts.summary: Pentz as governor of Glückstadt writes to the King about a letter to His Majesty, Hamburg, men come in, and asks for an admiral, timber from Norway, provisions, gunners and fireworkers for the fortress; probably early 1630, when the Elbe dispute with Hamburg led to a fleet under an admiral. Holes in most sentences.
texts.note: read_share is the strict first-pass share: 25 of 68 units (36.76%). Marked 'decoded, not read' because most sentences have holes; the reviewer may judge otherwise.

outcome.notes: No docs/_validate.py run (repository scripts not run by the contributor). Figures per document; the two letters are not pooled. Key v2 (key_history/KEY_pentz_v2_b110.txt) is filed for the record and not used.
